findings.issue: An object-valued position/situation (e.g. {"toString": 1}) makes echo()'s String(value) throw a raw TypeError, not a StyleValidationError. The same applies to String(data.justification) at the found.set call. Import still fails closed, but the message lists none of the file's problems.
findings.evidence: Style JSON is bundled, authored data (spec §8), not user input. startingRange[i].position = {"toString":1} -> echo(data.position) -> String() throws TypeError. No untrusted path reaches this. echo is pre-existing; this change adds new call sites for it.
findings.fix: Optional: in echo, use typeof value === 'string' ? value : JSON.stringify-ish/typeof label, or wrap String() in try/catch.

summary: No BLOCKER/MAJOR. The startingRange validator matches tokens by Array.includes against the fixed 169-entry HAND_CLASSES list, so prototype keys like __proto__ and constructor are rejected as unknown. Positions and situations are matched by strict equality against APPLICABLE_SPOTS['6-max'], so unknown spots are reported and skipped. Echoes are cut to 20 characters. split(/\s+/) runs in linear time (no ReDoS). Only authored, bundled files reach this code. Every problem is collected and the import fails closed. decideRock reads only the PlayerView. Preflop out-of-range hands return fold/check taken from view.legalActions, and in-range or postflop hands return recommend().move. The 'as Action' cast would hide an undefined if fold/check were missing, but the engine always offers fold when a bet is owed and check when none is, so that path isn't reachable. The worker matches exactly 'Rock' and everything else falls through to TAG as before. No randomness, no new dependencies, no secrets. rock.json's descriptions and justifications are original prose (REQ-061).
